canada.summary: John Tory has run Canada’s largest city, led the Progressive Conservative Party of Ontario and been a political strategist and adviser throughout his decades-long career.

canada.title: This McMaster University Lab is looking to lower the costs of medications. Here’s how
canada.summary: Inside the halls of McMaster University sits a laboratory researching how to optimize the manufacturing of therapeutic medications and, in turn, potentially lower the costs passed on to patients.

canada.title: RMs hope call for cell service goes through
canada.summary: BRANDON — Ernie Sirski jokes the only way he gets cell service is by standing on his tractor as he hold his phone in one hand and a pipe wrench in the other.

canada.title: What's in Ottawa's new forestry plan? Feds aim to reshape industry
canada.summary: Natural Resources Minister Tim Hodgson said Friday the blueprint, backed by a $6.5 billion funding plan, represents the largest federal investment in the industry's history. "Business as usual is not an option," he said.

canada.title: Alberta charity Parachutes for Pets says losing provincial funding means it's at risk of shutting down
canada.summary: Parachutes for Pets, an Alberta charity that supports low-income and vulnerable pet owners, says it's at risk of shutting down after learning it won't receive $600,000 in funding from the provincial government.

canada.title: The world’s 1st pro curling league is coming to Moose Jaw
canada.summary: Moose Jaw's deep-rooted curling culture is taking the spotlight as the city prepares to host Rock League in January.

canada.title: Regina movie fanatic who used to work at Blockbuster opens in-home video store
canada.summary: Physical media is back in style, according to stores in Regina, with more young people being attracted to older formats.

canada.title: Like sand through an hourglass, time is ticking down in Manitoba's silica-mining race
canada.summary: There's a race underway to mine Manitoba's ancient sand and convert the fine-grained silica that makes up most of it into materials that can be used in solar panels, superconductors and all manner of other industrial products in somewhat short supply around the world.

canada.title: Quebec parents pull children from elementary school over bullying, alleged death threats
canada.summary: Parents in Hemmingford, Que., are speaking out after they say their children were the target of bullying and death threats. They say they don't feel safe sending them to school anymore, considering what they qualify as an inadequate response from both the school and school board.

canada.title: What time is it? Ask the Beaverbrook Art Gallery's 24-hour movie exhibit
canada.summary: The 24-hour video installation by Swiss-American artist Christian Marclay is now at the Fredericton gallery. It's made of about 12,000 clips from movies and TV shows, each one showing or mentioning a time, and it plays in sync with the real time of day.

canada.title: Some N.S. woodlot owners 'skeptical' of proposed forestry federation
canada.summary: With some members of the province’s forestry sector promoting a new approach for representation, the executive director of the Nova Scotia Woodlot Owners and Operations Association says his board members are “very skeptical” of the proposal.

canada.title: 'There's a lot of good people': Man who faced homelessness seeks change in attitudes about emergency shelters
canada.summary: Corner Brook's Shawn Bennett will soon be settled in his own apartment after being homeless for more than eight months. He and shelter workers with a non-profit say high rent prices and low income support benefits are leading to more homelessness in the western Newfoundland city.

canada.title: They gave birth in the south. Now, they're helping Inuit deliver closer to home
canada.summary: Margaret Tukkiapik and Kayla Annanack-Lauzon study through the Puvirnituq Inuulitsivik Health Centre's midwifery program to provide prenatal, labour and post-natal care for Inuit who would otherwise travel outside of their region, culture and language.

canada.title: Temporary release of man who murdered 10-year-old girl cancelled, say Victoria police
canada.summary: The Victoria Police Department says the planned temporary release of a convicted child killer to attend cooking classes has been "indefinitely suspended."

lines: Good morning. I’m Hannah Thibedeau, and this is your Palindrome News brief.
One person is dead and several others are being treated in hospital following a four-vehicle crash on Highway 403 west of Garden Avenue Friday evening, The Canadian Press reports.

The Supreme Court of Canada has upheld Quebec’s secularism law and its use of the notwithstanding clause – as Saskatchewan waits to have its own case heard in the new year, The Canadian Press reports.
Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre is heading to Washington next week as trade talks between Canada and the United States continue, The Canadian Press reports.

The federal government says seven teams have been selected to take part in a design competition to restore the prime minister’s official residence at 24 Sussex Drive in Ottawa, The Canadian Press reports.
The CRTC issued a ruling Friday saying that carriers violated its prohibition on charging a fee for providing and setting up cellphones when signing up for a service plan, The Canadian Press reports.
Uganda begins Africa’s first mRNA Ebola vaccine trial, Euronews reports.
That’s your brief. We’ll keep watching, so you don’t have to.
